newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia skilled vacancies falls in June.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia skilled vacancies falls in June.

text.p: The Australian Government's skilled vacancies index fell 0.7 percent in June from May and was unchanged from a year earlier, the Employment Department said on Thursday.
The department said the latest monthly fall continued the downward trend of recent months, which has seen the index fall steadily to 144 from 149 in February.

Increases were recorded in five of the 16 occupational groups, with the biggest rise a 9.6 percent jump for the medical and science technical officers grouping. Building trades were up 5.7 percent in the month and natural scientists 2.5 percent.

The strongest falls among the 11 groups which declined were a 6.1 percent drop in the health diagnosis and treatment practitioners sector, 5.0 percent in engineering and building associates and technicians and 4.8 percent in vehicle trades.
The monthly index is 118.2 percent above the recession low of 66 in mid-1991.
Only two states recorded an increase -- Queensland with 2.4 percent and Western Australia with 0.9 percent.
All other states and the Northern Territory fell, with the biggest decline a 9.3 percent drop in the Northern Territory and a 5.4 percent fall in Tasmania.
However, the department cautions the territory's results are highly volatile because of the small sample.
The monthly index is based on a count of skilled vacancies advertisements in the major metropolitan newspaper for each state captal and the Northern Territory.
